findings: Distinguishes the 2004 study scope from the 2002 clustering article and describes literature-informed proposed groupings.
Sample size alone does not establish representativeness or reliability.
The broad program approach is distinct from the specific four-dimension CQ model.

Meeting participation alone does not establish psychological safety or explain prior silence.
Formal Tribal consultation is distinct from routine planning or liaison participation.
Historical samples and community briefs do not substitute for individual perspectives.
